description: Evaluates extracted scientific conclusions for papers scoring > 50 points. Assesses cross-paper consensus, underlying paper quality, clinical relevance, dosage feasibility, and safety.

confidence_bands.label: Gold Standard Claim — High Confidence
confidence_bands.description: Strongly supported by multiple high-grade papers with high consensus, clinically meaningful human effect sizes, and realistic oral dosage.

confidence_bands.label: Promising Evidence — Moderate Confidence
confidence_bands.description: Supported by good quality research with majority agreement, though minor contradictory evidence or smaller sample sizes exist.

confidence_bands.label: Preliminary / Conditional Claim
confidence_bands.description: Based on moderate paper scores or proxy markers, or inconsistent results across different human trials.

confidence_bands.label: Weak or Contradicted Claim
confidence_bands.description: Heavily disputed by higher-grade studies, based on unrealistic dosing, or lacking direct human outcome data.

confidence_bands.label: Refuted or Unsafe Claim
confidence_bands.description: Directly debunked by high-quality meta-analyses or carries unacceptable toxicity/safety risks.

categories.label: Source Paper Quality Base
categories.description: Base score proportional to the parent paper's grade score (e.g. paper score of 80/100 contributes 20 points). Papers with grade score <= 50 are excluded entirely.

score_tiers.example: Extracted from an 'A' grade paper (score 85-100)
Extracted from a 'B' grade paper (score 70-84)
Extracted from a 'C' grade paper (score 51-69)

categories.label: Cross-Paper Consensus & Contradiction
categories.description: Evaluates agreement vs. dissent across all other retrieved papers for the ingredient, weighted by those papers' respective grades.

score_tiers.example: Strong consensus — multiple other Grade A/B papers corroborate this conclusion with zero major contradictions.
Moderate agreement — other papers support the claim, but sample sizes or populations differ slightly.
Isolated claim — no other papers confirm or contradict it yet.
Minor contradiction — lower-grade or equivalent papers find conflicting results.
Direct refutation — higher-grade meta-analyses or RCTs explicitly contradict this conclusion.

categories.label: Clinical Relevance & Direct Outcome
categories.description: Measures whether the conclusion proves a direct human health outcome or merely an indirect biological biomarker.

score_tiers.example: Direct, measurable human efficacy (e.g. reduced pain, improved sleep efficiency)
Surrogate clinical endpoint in humans (e.g. lowered blood pressure, improved lipid profile)
Indirect biomarker or mechanism in healthy human volunteers
In vitro mechanism, cell culture, or animal tissue response

categories.label: Dosage & Bioavailability Realism
categories.description: Assesses if the effective concentration mentioned in the conclusion translates to a realistic, oral daily supplement dosage.

score_tiers.example: Standard oral supplementation dose (e.g. 100mg - 500mg daily) with proven oral bioavailability
High but achievable oral dose (e.g. 1g - 3g daily) or requires specialized delivery (liposomal)
Unclear dosing mentioned in conclusion
Unrealistic or unsafe dose (e.g. 50g/day needed orally) or IV-only administration

categories.label: Safety & Side Effect Profile
categories.description: Rewards claims that confirm strong safety thresholds and penalizes conclusions associated with severe side effects.

score_tiers.example: Conclusion explicitly documents well-tolerated safety profile and zero adverse events
Mild, reversible side effects reported (e.g. slight stomach upset)
Safety outcomes not measured or reported in conclusion
Reported organ toxicity, severe contraindications, or drug-interaction hazards
